Q1: o-Xylene's hazard profile indicates known significant hazards (Tier 1) across several categories, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental, inhalation, oral, and organ/systemic hazards. Dermal and eye hazards have an expanded perspective classification (Tier 2), while endocrine disruption hazards remain data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: o-Xylene is recognized on key regulatory lists of concern in the United States. Specifically, it is listed under the Clean Water Act as a hazardous substance and as a Hazardous Air Pollutant by the EPA.
Q3: o-Xylene is extensively characterized, supported by approximately 36,000 literature references, significantly higher than the median for similar chemicals. Its specific molecular formula (C8H10) and classification as a "Small Molecule," rather than an Incompletely Defined Substance (UVCB), further confirm its well-defined nature. The presence of only one data-deficient hazard class (EDC4) also indicates a largely complete hazard assessment.
